title: Unify GPU nodegroup scaling policy for ASG and Karpenter in private VPC
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Background: private VPC customers run heterogeneous GPU fleets. Today we have two parallel IaC patterns: ASG-backed gpu nodegroups (legacy) and Karpenter-based ephemeral GPU nodes. Both use separate Terraform modules and diverging autoscale/safety policies which increases operational burden and causes rollout drift during driver/kernel upgrades.

Goal: Build a Terraform-level policy unifier and module wrapper that emits consistent scaling and safety primitives for both ASG and Karpenter flows. The unified approach must: 1) expose a single configuration surface for safety windows, health-check frequency, drain/grace periods, and upgrade batches; 2) synthesize the appropriate resources (ASG launch configs, autoscaling policies, Karpenter Provisioner CR integrations) without duplicating logic in consumers; 3) include Terraform validation tests and a CI plan that runs in the private-VPC environment; 4) provide canary rollout and automatic drift detection for nodegroup spec vs. live state.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change pricing or core runtime kernel selection; it avoids rearchitecting the serving runtime scheduler.

Acceptance criteria:
- terraform module "redwood/gpu-node-fabric" publishes inputs: gpu_type, min/max/desired, scaling_policy, upgrade_batch_size, health_probe_interval, drain_timeout, allow_spot_fallback.
- Module can produce both: ASG nodegroup (with lifecycle hooks, SSM-based preflight, and instance profile) AND Karpenter Provisioner integration (via k8s_manifest/provider blocks) from the same inputs.
- End-to-end CI: Terraform plan/apply runs against a private dev VPC (test harness) and validates that nodes join the cluster, kubelet labels are applied, and a workload eviction+recreate passes under a simulated GPU driver upgrade.
- Observability: new dashboards and alerts for node-repair-rate, time-to-replace, and scaling-error-rate exist in the private-console team dashboard.
- Rollout strategy documented (confluence) and a staged canary deploy having automated rollback on increased eviction/failed-provisioning rate.

Design notes / constraints:
- Prefer helper locals and single-source-of-truth templating in Terraform (avoid module duplication). Use terraform 1.6+ language features (dynamic blocks, for_each on maps) to generate resources.
- For Karpenter, avoid coupling to a specific CRD schema version; use a light transform step in the module to render provisioner YAML via templatefile and k8s_manifest (resource provider).
- For ASG path, include lifecycle hook to run a healthcheck script (SSM) that reports to a DynamoDB-backed repair-queue; ensure instance termination is gated by success/failure signals to avoid premature drains.
- Health checks: default to 30s probe interval, 3 consecutive failures → mark unhealthy. Allow customers to tune via module input.
- Upgrade strategy: support rolling batches with a concurrent-drain limit, and a fallback policy to spin up CPU-only nodes when GPU nodes fail provisioning to preserve SLOs.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increased Terraform module complexity vs. improved maintainability. We must guard against long plan times by using count/for_each conservatively.
- Karpenter dynamic nature makes deterministic terraform planning harder; rely on post-deploy convergence checks and CI gating.
- Operational complexity for SSM+DynamoDB repair-queue needs runbook and oncall integration.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Draft module API and publish RFC in Confluence (milestone: 2026-02-20) — DONE.
2) Implement core locals & config mapping to ASG and Provisioner templates (sprint 1).
3) Add lifecycle hooks/SSM scripts and DynamoDB repair-queue (sprint 2).
4) Add CI e2e harness (terraform apply on dev VPC) and golden tests that simulate driver upgrade.
5) Instrument dashboards & alerts, and run canary on a subset of clusters.

Notes on testing: The e2e harness will create a small private dev VPC to avoid billing surprises, and will reuse existing small-spot GPU SKU images. Tests include: kubelet label reconciliation, pod scheduling on GPUs, graceful evictions during drain, and simulated provisioning failures that verify automatic fallback to CPU nodes.

Migration plan: provide a migration script that reads old module outputs and translates them to the new unified inputs, then run in dry-run mode with diffs and operator review before apply.

2026-02-22 - Marco Chen: Spike complete for templatefile approach. Proof-of-concept repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-gpu-fabric/pull/12. Observed terraform plan times increased by ~12% when provisioning both ASG and k8s_manifest resources — will optimize locals.
2026-02-28 - SRE Oncall (Priya Rao): Healthcheck design approved; asked to add metric 'node_repair_latency_ms' and an SLO target. Also requested an ops runbook (linked below).

2026-03-03 - Marco Chen: Implemented lifecycle hook + SSM script. Hook sends signal to DynamoDB; repair-queue lambda exists in sandbox account. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-gpu-fabric/pull/28
2026-03-07 - QA (Daniel Park): E2E harness fails when Karpenter provisioner uses capacityType: spot — intermittent provisioning timeouts. Added test to force main path on-demand for reliability.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Verma: Added canary rollout plan to Confluence. CLI tool 'infra-migrate' will emit a dry-run migration plan and create a 'migration-checklist' issue for each cluster migrated.
next_steps:
- Complete terraform module refactor and reduce plan time by eliminating duplicate computed values.
- Finish CI e2e harness and wire it into private pipeline.
- Create runbook and schedule oncall playbook review with SRE.
- Run migration dry-runs on two non-prod clusters before canary rollout.
